h: Snow Days and West Yorkshire Extras
p: Indoor snow can feel a bit daunting if you've never tried it, but the slope is set up to ease people in gently. Beginners stay on the shallow lower section with an instructor, learning how to move, turn and stop safely before going any higher. Snowboarders, fair warning, spend more time on their bums in the early stages, so waterproof trousers are a real help.

Dress for real winter. It's kept below freezing, so bring gloves, a hat, thick socks and layers you can strip off if you warm up. Kit hire is commonly included with lessons, but do check exactly what's covered when you book, especially if you're bringing your own boots or helmet.

Once you've thawed out, the wider area has plenty to offer. The Hepworth Wakefield, a gallery beside the River Calder named after the sculptor Barbara Hepworth, is a short drive away and makes a calm, interesting stop. The Yorkshire Sculpture Park near West Bretton is a full day in itself, with huge works set out across rolling parkland, and it's free to walk round (you pay for parking).

Pontefract is just down the road too, with the ruins of its castle and a long tradition of liquorice growing that still gives the town its sweet reputation. Leeds is about twenty minutes away if anyone wants a city fix.

Snozone is a brilliant way to prepare for a ski trip, but it's also just good fun on its own. Book lessons early before February half-term and the Christmas holidays, which are prime time for families getting ready for the mountains.
